result: In a pilot (10 controls, 12 mild/moderate ME/CFS, 9 long COVID), hemodynamic responses to 5-min 70-degree tilt, hypoxia and hypercapnia did not differ from controls (p>0.05); ME/CFS showed greater fall in cerebrovascular resistance and impaired autoregulation during hypercapnia (p=0.041, 0.042) and impaired cognitive-motor integration (p<0.02).
reason: Measured cerebrovascular variables during tilt and found no group difference; weak contradiction given n=12, 5-min tilt vs 30-min protocols, and the abstract does not state tilt CBF values explicitly.

result: ME/CFS showed impaired cerebral autoregulation during 5% CO2 breathing; long COVID showed reduced peripheral and end-tidal oxygen and less vagal withdrawal on tilt; no end-tidal CO2 difference on tilt is reported.
reason: Abstract does not report end-tidal CO2 or hyperventilation during tilt; hypercapnic cerebrovascular reactivity is a different measure; the paper is already linked via neuro-cbf-tilt.

result: In 619,983 COVID-19 cases among US active-duty service members, 158 had a coded PASC dysautonomia diagnosis; white non-Hispanic ethnicity, female sex, younger age, northeast region, more severe COVID and comorbid depression/anxiety were associated risk factors.
reason: Diagnosis-code epidemiology of risk factors, not objective autonomic testing; does not measure what the finding claims.

result: In 1375 CDC-criteria CFS patients (1072 also NICE/IOM), fatigue severity was the only correlate of response inhibition, and fatigue plus pain severity, bodily pain and physical functioning correlated with slower Symbol Digit, motor speed and reaction time; associations with pain and function strengthened with age, not illness duration.
reason: Same speeded cognitive measures in a large cohort; adds symptom-severity correlates and age moderation (no control comparison).

result: [11C]K-2 PET showed brain-wide increased AMPA receptor density (SUVR-WM) in 30 long COVID patients with cognitive impairment vs 80 healthy controls, correlating positively with plasma TNFSF12 and negatively with CCL2; a PLS classifier reached 100% sensitivity and 91.2% specificity.
reason: Newer atlas id neuro-ampa-pet covers AMPA receptor PET; this is the long COVID version (if that finding already cites this study, drop as already cited); otherwise new neuro domain.

result: Of 467 non-hospitalised, highly symptomatic long COVID patients, 143 (31%) were diagnosed with POTS on tilt/active stand; POTS patients were younger, 91% female, less active and walked less on 6MWT (448 vs 472 vs 509 m).
reason: No cerebral blood flow or preload data, which is the core of this finding; prevalence is handled by the neuro-pots-prevalence link.

result: Of 467 non-hospitalised, highly symptomatic long COVID patients, 143 (31%) met POTS criteria on tilt/active stand (testing only in clinically suspected cases); POTS patients were younger, 91% female, less active, had higher 6MWT heart rates and shorter walk distance, with similar symptom profiles.
reason: Long COVID, not ME/CFS, so a long COVID version of the prevalence finding (31%, within the 6-43% range) rather than an independent replication.

result: In 54 hospitalised COVID-19 patients, higher acute-phase IL-1RA, IFN-gamma, TNF-alpha and monocyte percentage predicted greater physical and total fatigue 6-9 months later; higher TNF-alpha correlated with lower awareness of cognitive fatigue (r=-0.40, p=0.019).
reason: Same mechanism (acute cytokine response predicting later post-infective fatigue) extended to SARS-CoV-2; small hospitalised cohort, fatigue score outcome rather than CFS case definition.

result: Acute-phase IL-1RA, IFN-gamma, TNF-alpha and monocyte percentage predicted post-COVID fatigue at 6-9 months in 54 hospitalised patients.
reason: Acute-infection serum predictors, not immune profiling of established long COVID (T-cell exhaustion, EBV antibodies, cortisol); covered by the immune-sickness-behaviour link.

result: Meta-analysis (13 studies included; 5 studies, n=2261 for the main pool) found women with endometriosis had OR 2.79 (95% CI 2.00-3.89) for ME/CFS, and two studies of ME/CFS to endometriosis gave pooled OR 2.52 (2.45-2.60).
reason: Same endometriosis association, but a pooled meta-analysis that likely includes Boneva rather than an independent cohort; adds pooled estimate and bidirectionality.
